parts.text: 1. Word order is supplied explicitly because attention alone lacks recurrence and convolution.

citations.quote: we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence

parts.text: 2. Positional encodings are added directly to encoder and decoder input embeddings.

citations.quote: we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks

parts.text: 3. Each position receives a pattern of sine and cosine signals at different frequencies.

citations.quote: In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies

parts.text: 4. Sinusoidal encodings were chosen to help attention learn relative positions.

citations.quote: We chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions

parts.text: 5. Learned positional embeddings worked nearly as well as fixed sinusoidal encodings.

citations.quote: We also experimented with using learned positional embeddings [9] instead, and found that the two versions produced nearly identical results

parts.text: 6. Decoder masking preserves output order by blocking attention to future positions.

citations.quote: We also modify the self-attention sub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions

parts.text: 7. Masking and shifted embeddings restrict each prediction to earlier known outputs.

citations.quote: predictions for position i can depend only on the known outputs at positions less than i
